key_insight: Message-passing GNNs can approximate node centrality with strong ranking accuracy and transfer across unseen graph topologies, especially when trained on mixed graph distributions.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable alternative to exact centrality computation, with large reported speedups that could make graph analytics practical for larger systems and real-time workflows.
method: Supervised GNNs on exact betweenness/closeness centrality values
Frame centrality estimation as a node-ranking task and score with Kendall’s tau
Train on single- and mixed-distribution synthetic graphs to test transfer to unseen and real-world topologies
evidence_signal: On unseen Erdős–Rényi graphs, the models reach Kendall’s tau of 0.851 for betweenness and 0.894 for closeness, and a 5,000-node betweenness model reaches tau = 0.938 with up to 97.7x inference speedup.
watch_item: Closeness centrality appears more sensitive to community-structured and real-world graphs, so transfer may degrade when topology differs from the training distribution.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Scalable and Transferable Node Centrality Approximation
